We construct many new topological types of compact G 2 -manifolds, that is, Riemannian 7 -manifolds with holonomy group G 2 . To achieve this we extend the twisted connected sum construction first developed by Kovalev and apply it to the large class of asymptotically cylindrical Calabi–Yau 3 -folds built from semi-Fano 3 -folds constructed previously by the authors. In many cases we determine the diffeomorphism type of the underlying smooth 7 -manifolds completely; we find that many 2 -connected 7 -manifolds can be realized as twisted connected sums in a variety of ways, raising questions about the global structure of the moduli space of G 2 -metrics. Many of the G 2 -manifolds we construct contain compact rigid associative 3 -folds, which play an important role in the higher-dimensional enumerative geometry (gauge theory/calibrated submanifolds) approach to defining deformation invariants of G 2 -metrics. By varying the semi-Fanos used to build different G 2 -metrics on the same 7 -manifold we can change the number of rigid associative 3 -folds we produce.

1. Introduction In this paper we construct a large number of new compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds, that is Riemannian 7-manifolds ( M , g ) (M,g) whose holonomy group is the compact exceptional Lie group G 2 \textup{G}_{2} , using the so-called twisted connected sum construction; since any G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifold is Ricci-flat this yields many Ricci-flat metrics on compact 7 7 -manifolds. As an alternative to Joyce’s original pioneering construction of compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds via “orbifold resolutions” [ 41 , 42 ] , Kovalev (based on a suggestion of Donaldson) developed the twisted connected sum construction [ 44 ] as a way to obtain a compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifold by combining a pair of (exponentially) asymptotically cylindrical (ACyl) Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds. Loosely speaking, this method seeks to construct G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds that contain a sufficiently long almost cylindrical neck-like region; in this sense it resembles familiar “stretching the neck” constructions in a number of other geometric PDE problems. Kovalev constructed about one hundred ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds for use in twisted connected sums by starting from Fano 3-folds. In [ 18 ] we exhibited at least several hundred thousand families of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds built using weak Fano 3 3 -folds. We identify a subclass of “semi-Fano” 3-folds that have a well-behaved deformation theory, which we use to prove that ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds obtained from semi-Fanos can be “matched” to form twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –manifolds. In doing so we address some errors in [ 44 ] detailed below. Starting from semi-Fanos instead of Fanos lets us construct many more examples of compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –manifolds, and in many cases also makes it possible to exhibit compact associative submanifolds. Associative submanifolds G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds have two natural classes of interesting calibrated submanifolds: 3 3 -dimensional associative submanifolds and 4 4 -dimensional coassociative submanifolds. Constructing associative 3 3 -folds in compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds is difficult and relatively few examples are known; part of the difficulty is that—unlike that of its calibrated cousins: special Lagrangians or coassociatives—the deformation theory of compact associative 3 3 -folds can be obstructed. In many of the G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds we construct we can exhibit a finite number of rigid—and therefore unobstructed—associative 3 3 -folds diffeomorphic to 𝕊 1 × 𝕊 2 \mathbb{S}^{1}\times\mathbb{S}^{2} ; the use of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds constructed from semi-Fano (rather than Fano) 3 3 -folds is crucial here. The associative 3 3 -folds we construct are the first compact associative 3 3 -folds in compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds that are proven to be rigid. Thus our work yields a large number of compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds in which we can attempt to “count” associative 3 3 -folds—in the spirit of the higher-dimensional invariants envisioned in the papers of Donaldson-Thomas [ 27 ] and Donaldson-Segal [ 28 ] . In a related aspect of this programme, Walpuski [ 72 ] has recently shown how one can construct G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -instantons that “bubble” at suitable rigid associative submanifolds, reversing the fundamental bubbling analysis of Tian [ 69 ] . The topology of twisted connected sums We obtain detailed topological information about G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds of twisted connected sum type under certain mild extra assumptions on the building blocks used (which we show are satisfied in many cases). Joyce and Kovalev had been able to compute the fundamental group and the Betti numbers of the 7 7 -manifolds appearing in their constructions, but not further topological information; in particular not even the integral cohomology was known for their examples. We compute the full integral cohomology of many of our G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds including determining the torsion in H 3 H^{3} and H 4 H^{4} and also the characteristic class p 1 p_{1} , using topological information about the ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds from [ 18 ] . Calculating characteristic classes of a manifold constructed by gluing can be quite difficult, but the twisting in the twisted connected sum construction is sufficiently mild that we can get a handle on p 1 p_{1} . By distinguishing between examples with the same Betti numbers but different torsion or different p 1 p_{1} we are able to prove the existence of many new compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds. The twisted connected sum construction often yields 2 2 -connected 7 7 -manifolds, whereas Joyce’s “orbifold resolution” constructions typically yield 7 7 -manifolds with relatively large second Betti number (only a single example in Joyce’s book [ 42 ] has b 2 = 0 b^{2}=0 , see Remark 4.30 ). Using the classification theory for 2 2 -connected 7 7 -manifolds developed by Wall and Wilkens [ 74 ] , the topological data we have computed determines completely the diffeomorphism (or almost-diffeomorphism) type of many of the smooth 7 7 -manifolds on which we construct our G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -holonomy metrics; these are the first compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds for which the diffeomorphism type is known. These smooth 7 7 -manifolds have simple topological realisations as connected sums of a nontrivial 𝕊 3 \mathbb{S}^{3} -bundle over 𝕊 4 \mathbb{S}^{4} with an appropriate number of copies of 𝕊 3 × 𝕊 4 \mathbb{S}^{3}\times\mathbb{S}^{4} . This is one of very few instances of geometrically interesting 2 2 -connected 7 7 -manifolds for which the computations needed to determine the (almost) diffeomorphism classification have actually been carried out. Even in the simplest case where we use a pair of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds constructed from rank one Fano 3 3 -folds—as considered in Kovalev’s original twisted connected sum construction—our refined topological results allow us to prove a variety of new results. For instance in Section 7 we will show the following • The simplest matching between such ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds leads to 2 2 -connected G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds with torsion-free cohomology, in which case b 3 b^{3} is the only Betti number we need to consider; 46 46 different possible values of b 3 b^{3} are realised this way. • By distinguishing between examples with the same Betti numbers but different p 1 p_{1} we show that at least 82 82 different smooth 7 7 -manifolds are realised this way. • Using the classification theory for 2 2 -connected 7 7 -manifolds we determine the homeomorphism type of all these 7 7 -manifolds and in the majority of cases the diffeomorphism type. • We exhibit a pair of G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds whose underlying 7 7 -manifolds we prove to be homeomorphic but not necessarily diffeomorphic; this raises the question whether there exist different smooth structures on the same topological 7 7 -manifold which each admit G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -holonomy metrics. To determine the diffeomorphism types of this pair of 7 7 -manifolds requires the calculation of an extension of the classical Eells–Kuiper invariant, as will be discussed in [ 21 ] . We suspect that these 7-manifolds are in fact diffeomorphic. • Other possible ways to match such ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds exist and lead to simply-connected 7 7 -manifolds with H 2 = 0 H^{2}=0 but with non-trivial torsion in H 3 H^{3} ; at least 41 41 other topological types of G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifold arise in this way. The last point illustrates a general phenomenon: it is often possible to arrange matching between the same pair of building blocks in various ways and thereby to obtain topologically distinct 7 7 -manifolds from the same pair of blocks. The same techniques applied to more general ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds constructed from other Fano 3 3 -folds or more generally semi-Fano 3 3 -folds (or the Kovalev-Lee examples arising from non-symplectic involutions on K3s [ 45 ] ) allow us to construct a variety of new topological types of compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds. Many of the examples built using semi-Fano 3 3 -folds also contain compact rigid associative 3 3 -folds. Different G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -metrics on the same manifold? In the opposite direction using the diffeomorphism classification of 2 2 -connected smooth 7 7 -manifolds we show the following: there exist many 2 2 -connected smooth 7 7 -manifolds that arise as the underlying smooth manifold for G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds of twisted connected sum-type but in several (sometimes many) different ways. In other words, the twisted connected sum of different pairs of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds can often yield the same underlying smooth 7 7 -manifold. This phenomenon already occurs when matching pairs of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds constructed from rank one Fano 3 3 -folds as above. More generally, using ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds constructed from semi-Fano 3 3 -folds we can construct diffeomorphic G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds containing different numbers of obvious rigid associative 3 3 -folds. These facts naturally suggest the following: Question. When do these G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -metrics on the same 7 7 -manifold belong to different connected components of the moduli space of G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -metrics? While answering this question currently goes beyond the techniques we have available to us, it provides a further strong impetus for developing the higher-dimensional enumerative invariants proposed by Donaldson. A more elementary tool for distinguishing between components of the moduli space is to study the homotopy classes of G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –structures; however, it appears that in our examples of diffeomorphic G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –manifolds one can always choose the diffeomorphism so that their G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –structures are homotopic ( ie connected by a continuous path of G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –structures without any constraint on the torsion) [ 22 ] . Twisted connected sums and hyper-Kähler rotations To describe some other features of the paper we need to recall the basic ingredients involved in the twisted connected sum construction. In order to construct a metric g g with Riemannian holonomy the full group G 2 \textup{G}_{2} and not a smaller subgroup the underlying compact 7 7 -manifold M M must have finite fundamental group. Given a pair of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds V + V_{+} and V − V_{-} we need a way to glue the two non-compact 7 7 -manifolds M + = 𝕊 1 × V + M_{+}=\mathbb{S}^{1}\times V_{+} and M − = 𝕊 1 × V − M_{-}=\mathbb{S}^{1}\times V_{-} to get such a compact 7 7 -manifold. By construction the ends of our ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds have the form ℝ + × 𝕊 1 × S ± \mathbb{R}^{+}\times\mathbb{S}^{1}\times S_{\pm} where S ± S_{\pm} are smooth K3 surfaces. The obvious connected sum construction would yield a manifold with infinite fundamental group which could not admit a metric of full holonomy G 2 \textup{G}_{2} . Instead we choose to identify the cross-section of our ends 𝕋 2 × S ± \mathbb{T}^{2}\times S_{\pm} using a diffeomorphism which exchanges the two circle factors of 𝕋 2 \mathbb{T}^{2} . However, in order to get a well-defined G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -structure on M M we also need to identify the two K3 surfaces S ± S_{\pm} using a special diffeomorphism r : S + → S − \matheur{r}:S_{+}\rightarrow S_{-} . The K3 surfaces S ± S_{\pm} inherit hyper-Kähler structures from the geometry at infinity of V ± V_{\pm} , which can be defined in terms of a Ricci-flat metric and a triple of parallel complex structures I ± , J ± , K ± I_{\pm},J_{\pm},K_{\pm} . We need to construct a diffeomorphism r \matheur{r} which is an isometry and satisfies r ∗ I − = J + , r ∗ J − = I + , and hence r ∗ K − = − K + . \matheur{r}^{*}I_{-}=J_{+},\quad\matheur{r}^{*}J_{-}=I_{+},\quad\text{and hence}\quad\matheur{r}^{*}K_{-}=-K_{+}. We call such a map a hyper-Kähler rotation . Even given a plentiful supply of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds it is highly non-trivial to construct pairs of V ± V_{\pm} for which there is such a hyper-Kähler rotation r \matheur{r} . However, as soon as we can construct a hyper-Kähler rotation r \matheur{r} for a pair of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds V ± V_{\pm} we can use r \matheur{r} to form a twisted connected sum 7 7 -manifold M ​ r M{r} , and build on it a closed G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -structure which has small torsion. The perturbation theory for closed G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -structures developed by Joyce (or the specific ACyl version proved by Kovalev) therefore shows that we can then choose an appropriate small perturbation to yield a metric with holonomy G 2 \textup{G}_{2} on M ​ r M{r} . Thus two main steps are needed to implement the twisted connected sum construction: (i) Construct (families of) exponentially ACyl Calabi-Yau structures on suitable smooth quasiprojective 3 3 -folds. (ii) Understand how to find ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds for which there exists a hyper-Kähler rotation, within a given pair of families. We explain below in more detail how together with [ 18 ] and [ 37 ] this paper addresses problems with both steps (i) and (ii) in Kovalev’s original paper [ 44 ] —and therefore puts the twisted connected sum construction on a firm foundation—and also extends substantially the settings in which solutions to (i) and (ii) can be constructed. Exponentially ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds There are two ingredients, one analytic and one complex algebraic, for producing exponentially ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds. The analytic ingredient is to solve the complex Monge-Ampère equation on suitable smooth quasiprojective varieties and to obtain sufficiently strong estimates for these solutions. The proof of the exponential asymptotics of solutions to the complex Monge-Ampère equation in [ 44 ] is not valid, but a complete, short self-contained proof of the existence of exponentially asymptotically cylindrical Calabi-Yau metrics was given recently in [ 37 ] . With a suitable analytic existence theory in place the remaining complex algebraic task is to find a (large) supply of suitable quasiprojective varieties. ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds from Fano and weak Fano 3 3 -folds In [ 44 ] Kovalev showed how to construct some suitable quasiprojective 3 3 -folds by blowing up special curves (the smooth base locus of a sufficiently generic anticanonical pencil) in smooth Fano 3 3 -folds and removing a smooth anticanonical divisor. Recall a smooth Fano 3 3 -fold F F is a smooth projective variety for which − K F -K_{F} is ample or positive. There are exactly 105 deformation families of smooth Fano 3 3 -folds: complex projective space ℙ 3 \mathbb{P}^{3} , smooth quadrics, cubics and quartics in ℙ 4 \mathbb{P}^{4} being the simplest examples. We call the ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds obtained this way ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds of Fano type . A smooth weak Fano 3 3 -fold is a smooth projective variety for which the anticanonical bundle is big and nef (but not ample). Differential geometers are encouraged to think of a big and nef line bundle as the algebraic-geometric formulation of the line bundle admitting a hermitian metric whose curvature is sufficiently semi-positive. There are at least hundreds of thousands of deformation families of smooth weak Fano 3 3 -folds and the topology of smooth weak Fano 3 3 -folds is less restrictive than for Fano 3 3 -folds; unlike the Fano case there is at present no classification theory for weak Fano 3 3 -folds, except under very special geometric assumptions, but many examples are known. In our paper [ 18 ] we proved that one can construct suitable quasiprojective 3-folds from any weak Fano 3 3 -fold (satisfying one further very mild assumption); combining this weak Fano construction with the analytic existence results from [ 37 ] we thereby increased the number of known ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds from a few hundred to several hundred thousand. We call these ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds of weak Fano type . Constructing hyper-Kähler rotations With a plentiful supply of exponentially asymptotically cylindrical Calabi-Yau 3-folds now at hand, to complete the twisted connected sum construction it remains to solve (ii): find pairs of (families) of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds for which there exists a hyper-Kähler rotation. In [ 44 ] Kovalev developed an approach to proving the existence of hyper-Kähler rotations between pairs of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds of Fano type. Unfortunately in almost all cases his argument relies on Lemma 6.47 in [ 44 ] which is false. In the course of the current paper we revisit carefully the construction of hyper-Kähler rotations, to correct, clarify and extend the methods available. In particular our results allow us to construct hyper-Kähler rotations for many pairs of (families) of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds of so-called semi-Fano type—a large subclass of weak Fano 3-folds described below. (After conversations with two of the present authors the final version of Kovalev-Lee [ 45 ] contains a similar construction of hyper-Kähler rotations for ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds of Fano or “nonsymplectic” type). We should point out immediately that given a pair of deformation families of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds V ± V_{\pm} there are typically various ways to construct hyper-Kähler rotations between the asymptotic ends ℝ + × 𝕊 1 × S ± \mathbb{R}^{+}\times\mathbb{S}^{1}\times S_{\pm} . The topology of the resulting 7 7 -manifold M M depends on the choice of the hyper-Kähler rotation r : S + → S − \matheur{r}\colon S_{+}\to S_{-} . At present we do not understand in a systematic way all possible different ways to match a given pair of (deformation families of) ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds V ± V_{\pm} ; however, we will exhibit various examples where several different matchings are possible and lead to topologically distinct G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds. In some simple cases we do understand essentially all different possible ways to match a given pair. Deformation theory for weak and semi-Fano 3-folds In Kovalev’s original approach to the construction of hyper-Kähler rotations between pairs of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds of Fano type the deformation theory for pairs ( F , S ) (F,S) where F ∈ ℱ F\in\mathcal{F} a deformation type of smooth Fano 3 3 -folds and S ∈ | − K F | S\in\lvert-K_{F}\rvert is a smooth anticanonical divisor plays a crucial role. Our approach to the construction of hyper-Kähler rotations also rests on a sufficiently good deformation theory: For pairs of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds of weak Fano (or Fano) type the construction of hyper-Kähler rotations is possible provided we have a sufficiently good deformation theory for pairs ( Y , S ) (Y,S) , where Y ∈ 𝒴 Y\in\mathcal{Y} , a given deformation type of weak Fano 3 3 -folds, and S ∈ | − K Y | S\in\lvert-K_{Y}\rvert is a smooth section. In [ 18 ] we showed that the deformation theory of such pairs is well-behaved for the subclass of semi-Fano 3 3 -folds. A semi-Fano 1 1 1 There seems to be no established terminology for this particular subclass of weak Fano 3-folds, so the term semi-Fano is our invention: it is intended to suggest that a semi-Fano 3-fold has semi- small anticanonical morphism. Warning: semi-Fano has also been used to mean something even weaker than weak Fano, ie a complex manifold for which − K Y -K_{Y} is nef (but not necessarily big), but this terminology is not well-established. 3 3 -fold is a weak Fano 3 3 -fold on which we impose an extra assumption on the geometry of its anticanonical morphism, namely that it contracts no divisor to a point. This assumption guarantees that certain cohomology vanishing theorems that are true for Fano 3 3 -folds (but which are false for general weak Fano 3 3 -folds) still hold for semi-Fano 3 3 -folds. There are still hundreds of thousands of deformation families of semi-Fano 3 3 -folds. We prove that we can construct hyper-Kähler rotations for pairs of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds of semi-Fano type under the same sorts of conditions as for pairs arising from (deformation types of) Fano 3 3 -folds. As we already explained, together with the constructions of [ 18 ] this immediately gives rise to many new twisted connected sum compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds. Using just ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds from Fano or semi-Fano 3 3 -folds of rank at most two or from toric semi-Fano 3-folds we get at least 50 million matching pairs (and probably many more) that produce 2-connected G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –manifolds. On the other hand, the smooth classification results show that the number of different topological types realised is much smaller, so as mentioned earlier some smooth 7-manifolds must arise as twisted connected sums in many different ways. Rigid curves and rigid associative 3 3 -folds There is one further immediate advantage of generalising from ACyl Calabi-Yau 3-folds of Fano type to those of semi-Fano type. If Y Y is a Fano 3 3 -fold then − K Y ⋅ C > 0 -K_{Y}\cdot C>0 for any algebraic curve C C and hence C C meets any anticanonical divisor S ∈ | − K Y | S\in\lvert-K_{Y}\rvert . However, semi-Fano 3 3 -folds can contain special complex curves C C for which K Y ⋅ C = 0 K_{Y}\cdot C=0 ; the weakening of − K Y -K_{Y} being positive to sufficiently semi-positive is crucial here. Moreover, in many cases C C is a smooth rational curve with normal bundle 𝒪 ⁡ ( − 1 ) ⊕ 𝒪 ⁡ ( − 1 ) \mathcal{O}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}(-1) : in this case C C is infinitesimally rigid, ie has no infinitesimal (holomorphic) deformations. Precisely because these special K Y K_{Y} -trivial curves are rigid and do not intersect anticanonical divisors we can use them to construct compact rigid holomorphic curves in our ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds. These rigid curves allow us to produce rigid associative 3 3 -folds diffeomorphic to 𝕊 1 × 𝕊 2 \mathbb{S}^{1}\times\mathbb{S}^{2} in our twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds. The key point is that we have related the deformation problem for a holomorphic curve C C to that of an associative of product form 𝕊 1 × C \mathbb{S}^{1}\times C . Algebraic geometry provides many tools to understand the deformation theory of C C ; for a general associative 3 3 -fold we have no such tools to understand its deformation theory. G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -transitions In the geometry of Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds, especially in some of their applications to String Theory, an important role is played by so-called geometric transitions . The simplest and most important such transitions are flops and conifold transitions . These two types of transitions also appear in the context of weak Fano 3 3 -folds; many smooth weak Fano 3 3 -folds can be flopped to yield other smooth weak Fano 3 3 -folds (which typically are not deformation equivalent to the original weak Fano 3 3 -fold). However, unlike the Calabi-Yau setting where the condition c 1 = 0 c_{1}=0 is preserved, a conifold transition that begins with a Fano 3 3 -fold F F will yield only a weak Fano 3 3 -fold Y Y . We can construct ACyl Calabi-Yau metrics on blocks constructed from both the Fano F F and the weak Fano Y Y , and then try to match both types of block to some other given (deformation family of) ACyl Calabi-Yau structure. This gives rise to the idea of related G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds or G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -transitions. For the moment we present G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -transitions as a convenient organisational principle that explains certain features of the geography of twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds. However, there is the future prospect of realising these G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -transitions at the level of metric geometry; we explain some of the technical difficulties that would need to be overcome to achieve this. Connections to M-theory G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –manifolds play a similar role in M-theory as Calabi-Yau 3-folds do in String Theory. Two questions of significance for M-theory concern the existence of coassociative K3-fibrations and singular G 2 \textup{G}_{2} –manifolds. Any twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifold is K3-fibred—essentially because the building blocks Z Z from which we construct our ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds are K3-fibred. Generically the only singular fibres of a building block Z Z , and therefore of our G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds, are A 1 A_{1} singularities. Because of subtleties due to the singular fibres it is still unknown if these topological “almost” coassociative K3-fibrations can be made into coassociative K3-fibrations as expected in [ 34 , 1 ] . To obtain realistic particle physics ( ie non-abelian gauge groups and chiral fermions) from M-theory on G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds it appears necessary to consider singular G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -spaces with very particular kinds of singularity as explained in [ 7 , 1 , 2 , 9 ] . For some recent physical predictions from M-theory on G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -spaces see [ 4 , 3 , 5 ] ; see also [ 10 , 24 , 64 , 35 , 61 , 6 ] for some other aspects of M-theory on G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -spaces. In the present paper we consider only smooth compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds (apart from the discussion in the G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -transitions section where we discuss potential ways to realise singular G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds as degenerate limits of our constructions). There are potential extensions of the present constructions that might in some circumstances allow the construction of blocks fibred by generically singular K3 fibres. However it is not yet clear that these could give rise to G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -spaces with the sort of singularity structure apparently required. It would be interesting to know: does the presence of torsion in H 3 H^{3} or H 4 H^{4} of a compact G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifold have any significance in M-theory? What if any significance do the G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -transitions discussed in Section 8 have in M-theory? Does the existence of many potentially different G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -metrics on the same smooth 7 7 -manifold have any M-theory interpretation? Structure of paper We now describe the structure of the rest of the paper. Section 2 reviews basic facts about the group G 2 \textup{G}_{2} , G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -structures, G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -holonomy metrics, the two natural calibrations on G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds and the relations to Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds, hyper-Kähler K3 surfaces and the groups SU ( 2 ) (2) and SU ( 3 ) (3) . We include this standard material for two reasons: to make the paper more accessible to readers with backgrounds in algebraic geometry or topology and also to establish the notation and the conventions we adopt in our paper. The reader familiar with the basics of G 2 G_{2} -holonomy metrics can safely skip most of this section. Section 3 introduces ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds and recalls how to construct them from certain algebro-geometric data that we call a building block . We recall Kovalev’s twisted connected sum construction : it takes a pair of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds together with the specification of a so-called hyper-Kähler rotation and produces a compact 7 7 -manifold M M with finite fundamental group and a 1 1 -parameter family of closed G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -structures on M M with small torsion. We explain how the known perturbation theory for closed G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -structures with small torsion allow us to construct a 1 1 -parameter family of G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -holonomy metrics on M M . In summary, this section reduces the problem of finding twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds to finding hyper-Kähler rotations between a given pair of (deformation families) of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds. Section 4 develops various tools to compute topological invariants of compact twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds building on results on the cohomology of the 6 6 -dimensional building blocks proved in [ 18 ] . Theorem 4.9 computes the integral cohomology groups of our twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds and proves under our assumptions that they are all simply-connected. In general there can be torsion in H 3 ​ ( M ) H^{3}(M) and H 4 ​ ( M ) H^{4}(M) ; we establish various restrictions on the possible torsion linking form of general twisted connected sums. We review the almost-diffeomorphism classification of closed 2 2 -connected 7 7 -manifolds including cases in which almost-diffeomorphism can be replaced with diffeomorphism. We explain a simple sufficient condition for our twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifold M M to be 2 2 -connected with torsion-free H 4 ​ ( M ) H^{4}(M) and then study the diffeomorphism and almost-diffeomorphism types of such 7 7 -manifolds. A key role is played by the divisibility of the first Pontrjagin class p 1 ​ ( M ) p_{1}(M) ; in turn the divisibility of p 1 ​ ( M ) p_{1}(M) is closely related to the divisibility of the second Chern class c 2 c_{2} of our building blocks, as studied in [ 18 ] . We apply all these results later to study the diffeomorphism type of concrete G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds constructed in Section 7 , but our methods apply to twisted connected sum manifolds more generally. Section 5 deals with the construction of associative submanifolds in our twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds. After recalling some basic features of the geometry of associative 3 3 -folds we prove Theorem 5.3 : this gives a general persistence result for a closed infinitesimally rigid associative 3 3 -fold A A under a small deformation of the G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -structure. Theorem 5.4 gives a generalisation in which we prove persistence of multi-parameter families of closed associative 3 3 -folds in a multi-parameter torsion-free deformation of the original G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -structure under a surjectivity assumption on the family. These results are extensions of the deformation theory established by McLean [ 50 , §5] . Next we consider the relation between associative 3 3 -folds in the product of a circle 𝕊 1 \mathbb{S}^{1} and a Calabi-Yau 3 3 -fold and holomorphic curves in the Calabi-Yau. This relation is fundamental to the construction of associative 3 3 -folds in many of our twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds. Particularly important is the simple observation—see Lemma 5.11 —that 𝕊 1 × C \mathbb{S}^{1}\times C is rigid as an associative 3 3 -fold if and only if C C is rigid as a holomorphic curve. Putting together the results from the section we prove Proposition 5.15 : each closed rigid holomorphic curve C C in one of our ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds can be perturbed to a compact rigid associative 3 3 -fold diffeomorphic to 𝕊 1 × C \mathbb{S}^{1}\times C in our twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifold for all sufficiently long “neck lengths”. With a little more work, we also show how to produce closed associative 3 3 -folds, including some non-rigid ones, in twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds from certain closed special Lagrangian 3 3 -folds in our ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds. Section 6 deals with the so-called “matching problem”, ie the construction of pairs of ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds with a hyper-Kähler rotation. Our approach to solving the matching problem requires some well-known facts about moduli spaces of lattice polarised K3 surfaces, the global Torelli theorem in this context and some results from deformation theory proved in [ 18 ] ; we review these very briefly. We describe in detail one general strategy which we call “orthogonal gluing” which yields solutions to the matching problem in a large number of cases. A special case of “orthogonal gluing” is what we term “primitive perpendicular gluing”. The benefit of “primitive perpendicular gluing” is that it is guaranteed to give a solution of the matching problem under the simple condition that the ranks of the Picard lattices of the deformation types 𝒴 ± \mathcal{Y}_{\pm} of semi-Fano 3 3 -folds used to construct the ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds add up to at most 11. Primitive perpendicular gluing enables us to mass-produce 2 2 -connected twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds and to understand their homeomorphism and diffeomorphism type in many cases. The more general “orthogonal gluing” produces manifolds M M with second Betti number b 2 ​ ( M ) > 0 b^{2}(M)>0 . It requires some sort of compatibility between the Picard lattices of the pair of semi-Fanos initially chosen and this does not always hold: see Example 6.8 . When it does hold, some further restrictions on the ranks of the Picard lattices allow the solution of the matching problem in this case: see Proposition 6.18 . In Section 7 we make examples of twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds—often containing compact rigid associative 3 3 -folds—and compute the topology of these examples. In this section we aim to give examples that illustrate the main points of what is achievable by the construction rather than to be systematic. Our examples are built mainly using specific ACyl Calabi-Yau 3 3 -folds of semi-Fano type which we constructed recently in [ 18 ] . Most of the examples we construct use perpendicular or orthogonal gluing. However, to demonstrate that these are labour-saving devices rather than a necessity we also consider what we have termed “handcrafted nonorthogonal gluing”. While this method applies in situations where “orthogonal gluing” fails it needs much more precise information about K3 moduli spaces and that information is usually very expensive to obtain. Therefore we give only a single example to illustrate the method and its potential complexities. In Section 8 we describe the more general possibilities and limitations of the construction and make some comments about the “geography” of examples that can be achieved by matching currently known pairs. The existing smooth classification theory for 7 7 -manifolds allows us to determine the diffeomorphism type of the majority of the 2 2 -connected twisted connected sums; to complete the diffeomorphism classification in the remaining 2 2 -connected cases we would need to be able to compute an extension of the classical Eells-Kuiper invariant. Moving beyond the 2 2 -connected world, we explain how to realise many simply-connected twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds with π 2 ​ ( M ) \pi_{2}(M) isomorphic to ℤ \mathbb{Z} or ℤ / k ​ ℤ \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z} and discuss the prospects for extending the smooth classification theory to cover these cases. Finally we discuss a way to organise various different twisted connected sum G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds constructed by matching pairs of Fano or semi-Fano 3 3 -folds related via flops or conifold transitions; by analogy we term these G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -transitions . We close by discussing the prospects for proving more precise topological and metric statements about G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -manifolds related by these G 2 \textup{G}_{2} -transitions.
